newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African money market unit trusts approved.
newsitem.headline: S.African money market unit trusts approved.

text.p: The development of South Africa's money market took another step forward on Tuesday when the parliamentary finance committee approved legislation to create unit trusts that invest exclusively in the money market.

Association of Unit Trusts chairman Carel de Ridder told Reuters that the first money market unit trust scheme could be operating by the end of the year if parliament passed the Unit Trusts Control Amendment Bill quickly.
"At this stage of the economic cycle when interest rates are high, it is a wonderful opportunity to be launching these unit trusts," he said.
Unit trusts would be able to invest in money market instruments of not more than 12 months' maturity.
Financial Services Board unit trusts manager Stiaan Hyman earlier told the committee that the new unit trusts would add to the rapid expansion of this business.

"There has been vast development in the unit trust industry over the last few years with assets growing to 40 billion rand by the end of June this year compared to 27 billion rand in June last year," he said.

An explanatory memorandum issued to the committee said that the new trusts would create an avenue for short-term investment, provide the sophistication of cash management to small investors and reduce risks.

De Ridder said that the new instruments would be invaluable to a wide range of small investors, including people who had accepted retrenchment packages and wanted to "park" their money somewhere for a short time while they set up a busines.
"An important feature of a money market fund is that its unit price does not vary, it stays fixed at one rand so it just earns interest," he said.
He said the industry first started examining money market funds four years ago.

"Our money market itself needs development," he said. "While the markets for treasury bills and bankers' acceptances are generally well developed, the market for issuing money market instruments by companies is not very well developed."

He said that he hoped the introduction of money market funds would lead to a renewed interest by companies in tapping the money market "because there is now another way of giving them access to the public's money as opposed to always simply going to borrow from the banks for funding the short term cash needs."
The Registrar of Unit Trust Companies had agreed to a standard application form for the funds and de Ridder said that the "only thing that could delay the process is technology".
"You need fairly sophisticated technology to be able to manage it successfully and cost effectively. So it will depend on the preparatory work that fund managers have done.
"Those that have been working on it in the last couple of months should be able to launch soon... we might have the first fund towards the end of this year."

De Ridder said that all legislation covering unit trusts was being reviewed by the association to make it more flexible and allow for the introduction of new unit trusts and other collective investment products.
